questions.q: If Surface tension$( S )$, Moment of Inertia $( I )$ and Planck's constant $( h ) ,$ were to be taken as the fundamental units, the dimensional formula for linear momentum would be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$P ∝ S^{a}I^{b}h^{c}$
$[ MLT^{- 1} ] = {\left[MT^{- 2}\right]}^{a}{\left[ML^{2}\right]}^{b}{\left[ML^{2}T^{- 1}\right]}^{C}$
\left[MLT^{- 1}\right] = [ M^{a + b + c}L^{2b + 2c}T^{- 2a - c} ]$
From comparing the power on both side
$a + b + c = 1$
$2b + 2c = 1$
$- 2a - c = - 1$
From the above three equations we will get
$a = \dfrac{1}{2}, b = \dfrac{1}{2} & c = 0$
$P ∝ S^{\dfrac{1}{2}}I^{\dfrac{1}{2}}h^{0}

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I List - II
a Torque i ${MLT}^{- 1}$
b Impulse ii ${MT}^{- 2}$
c Tension iii ${ML}^{2}T^{- 2}$
d Surface Tension iv ${MLT}^{- 2}$

Choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires& $ab, de$~and due to loop~$bcd$.

So,~${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} = {B}_{de}$~(directed out of the plane in both cases)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( 2\pi )$~(in the plane)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = - \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} + \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( 2\pi ) - \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{\mu0}{2\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi - 1 )$~ (III)

(B)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires~$ab, de$~and semicircular arc~$bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} = {B}_{de}$~(directed out of the plane in both cases)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$~(out of the plane)

Thus, net magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} + \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi ) + \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$

${B}_{0} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi + 2 )$~(I)

(C)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires~$ab, de$~and due to loop~$bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$~(directed in~the plane)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$~(in the plane)

${B}_{de} = 0$~(passing through the axis)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi + 1 )$~ (IV)

(D)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires~$ab, de$~and due to loop~$bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = 0 = {B}_{de}$~(passing through the axis)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{\mu0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$~(out of the plane)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}I}{4r}$& (II).

A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.q: The speed of a wave produced in water is given by $ν = {λ}^{a}g^{b}{ρ}^{c}$. Where $\lambda, g$ and $ρ$ are wavelength of wave, acceleration due to gravity and density of water respectively. The values of $a, b$ and $c$ respectively, are
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

The dimensional form of velocity can be written as

\left[v\right] = \left[{λ}^{a}g^{b}{ρ}^{c}\right]$

$⇒ \left[M^{0}LT^{- 1}\right] = \left[L\$right]a\left[$LT^{- 2}\right]b\left[ML^{- 3}\right]c$

Comparing the exponents for~$M, L, T$,

$ForM, M^{c} = M^{0}ForL, L^{a + b - 3c} = L^{1}ForT, T^{- 2b} = T^{- 1}$

So,

$c = 0 . . . ( i ) a + b - 3c = 1 . . . ( ii ) - 2b = - 1 . . . ( iii )$

From equations (i),(ii),(iii),

$a = \dfrac{1}{2},b = \dfrac{1}{2},c = 0

$

questions.q: An expression of energy density is given by $u = \dfrac{α}{β}sin \left(\dfrac{\alphax}{kt}\right), where \alpha, \beta~are constants, $x$ is displacement, $k$ is Boltzmann constant and $t$ is the temperature. The dimensions of \betawill be$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

Given that energy density& $U = \dfrac{α}{β}sin\dfrac{\alphax}{kt}$

As $\dfrac{\alphax}{kt}$~should be dimensionless, the dimensions of $\alphax$~and $kt$~should be same.

$⇒ \left[\alpha\right]\left[x\right] = \left[k\$right]\left[t\right] ⇒ \left[\alpha\right] =\left[k\right]\left[t\right]\left[x\right]$

Now,

\left[U\right] = \left[\alpha\right] \left[\beta\right]

$⇒ \left[\beta\right] = \left[\alpha\right]\left[$U\right] = \dfrac{\left[k\right] \left[t\right]}{ \left[x\right]\left[\dfrac{E}{V}\right]}$ = $\dfrac{ $\$left[\dfrac{E}{t}\right] \left[$t\$r$right]}${\left[x\$right]\left[\dfrac{E}{V}\right]}$

$⇒ \left[\beta\right] = \left[$L^{3}\right]\left[L\right] = \left[M^{0}L^{2}T^{0}\right]$

$

questions.q: \left(P + \dfrac{a}{V2}\right)\left(V - b\right) = RT$ represents the equation of state of some gases. Where $P$ is the pressure, $V$ is the volume, $T$ is the temperature and $a, b, R$ are the constants. The physical quantity, which has dimensional formula as that of $\dfrac{b2}{a}$ \text{ and } , will be :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the principle of dimensional homogeneity, the dimensions of each & terms of a dimensional equation on both sides are the same.

So,& dimension of& $b$~and $V$~will be same, \left[b\right] = \left[V\right]$~

And dimension of~\dfrac{a}{V2}~and~$P$~will be same,~ \left[\dfrac{a}{V2}\right] =\left[P\right]$

From above two relations, we have~ \left[\dfrac{a}{b2}\right] = \left[P\right]$

$∴ \left[\dfrac{b2}{a}\right] =1 \left[P\right] = \left[ML^{- 1}T^{- 2}\right]- 1$

Thus,~\left[M^{- 1}L^{1}T^{2}\right]$ is the dimension of compressibility.

questions.q: & The quantities $x = \dfrac{1}{{μ}_{0}{∈}_{0}}, y = \dfrac{E}{B}$~and~$z = \dfrac{l}{CR}$ are defined where C-capacitance, R-Resistance, $ℓ -$length, E-Electric field, B-magnetic field and$\in 0, \mu0, -$free space permittivity and permeability respectively. Then:
options: x, y and z have the same dimension.
Only x and z have the same dimension
Only x and y have the same dimension
Only y and z have the same dimension.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$(a) Dimensions of quantity are given bellow

${μ}_{0} = \left[TmA^{- 1}\right] = \left[Wbm^{- 1}A^{- 1}\right] = \left[Vsm^{- 1}C^{- 1}s\right] = \left[$NC^{- 2}s^{2}\right]{ε}_{0} = \left[$C^{2}N^{- 1}m^{- 2}\right]$

Now the dimension of~$x$~is given by

\left[$x\right] = $1\$left[\sqrt{{μ}_{0}{∈}_{0}}\right] = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{\left[NC^{- 2}s^{2}\right]\left[C^{2}N^{- 1}m^{- 2}\right]}}\left[x\right] = ms^{- 1}$

(b) The dimension of electric and magnetic field is given by,

$B = \left[$T\right] = \left[$Wbm^{- 2}\right] = \left[$Vsm^{- 2}\right]E = \left[$Vm^{- 1}\right]$

Now the dimension of~$y$~is given by,

~\left[$y\right] = \left[$E\right]\left[B\right] = \left[Vm^{- 1}\$right]\left[$Vsm^{- 2}\right] = ms^{- 1}$

(c) The dimension of capacitance~and resistance is given by,~

$C = \left[$CV^{- 1}\right]R = \left[$VC^{- 1}s\right]$

Now the dimension of~$z$~is given by

~\left[$z\right] = \left[$l\$right]\left[$CR\right] = \left[$m\right]\left[CV^{- 1}\right]\left[VC^{- 1}s\right] = ms^{- 1}

All quantities are having the dimensions of velocity.

$
